audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers disagreed on four of seven rows. content win[0..6] read Aurora seven times; full phases[N].side read Aurora, Aurora, Aurora, Skill, Skill, Kassadin, Kassadin. The packet also flags the content chart as impossible: Aurora wins 47.68% over 753 games but is credited with 7/7 stages.
audit.why: Kassadin is the archetype scaling matchup and the chart has to say so. Aurora owns levels 1 through first item: Null Sphere is 650 range against her 900, it costs him 60-80 mana, Nether Blade only empowers a melee auto, and Force Pulse needs charges before it fires in a 400 cone. Kassadin takes over once Riftwalk is rank 3 at a 2-second cooldown on a full build, with Void Stone reducing the magic damage Aurora answers with. A 47.68% win rate is exactly a lane won early and lost late.
audit.corrected: Aurora on rows 0-5, Kassadin on row 6. Full side edits for rows 3, 4 and 5; content win[6] flipped to Kassadin; ratings set 6/6/6/6/6/6/4; every why on a changed row rewritten in the same proposal.

audit.whatIsWrong: Content repeatedly treated Void Stone as an item ('built into Void Stone', 'gets Void Stone plus a full build'), and named 'Silence-lock' as Kassadin's late threat. breakdown.spikes and the phases whys were the generic Aurora template with no Kassadin content.
audit.why: Void Stone is Kassadin's passive: reduced magic damage taken and no unit collision. Riot's Null Sphere text is 'dealing damage and interrupting channels' — no silence appears anywhere in the kit, so 'Silence-lock' is not sourceable. His real ladder is Riftwalk 5s to 3.5s to 2s with escalating mana cost per repeat cast, and Force Pulse 21s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Void Stone named as the passive and used correctly (magic damage reduction, ignores unit collision); the late threat restated as chained 2-second Riftwalks for escalating damage; spike ladder rewritten around mana rather than an invented item.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page carried no ability interactions at all — every line was the Aurora template with Riftwalk's name pasted into it. Three real interactions were absent, and Aurora's E was again described as a 'knockback-slow'.
audit.why: enemyKit P: 'Kassadin takes reduced magic damage and ignores unit collision' — Aurora is a magic-damage champion and minions never body-block his walk-up. enemyKit Q: 'granting a temporary shield that absorbs magic damage' — that shield eats the front of Aurora's burst specifically. enemyKit E: 'Kassadin draws energy from spells cast in his vicinity' — Aurora's own poke charges Force Pulse. enemyKit W: autoReset flag plus 'next basic attack deals significant bonus magic damage' — the wind-up is the tell. ownerKit E: damage and slow, then Aurora hops backward; there is no knockback.
audit.corrected: All four now appear on the page: passive magic reduction and no unit collision, the magic shield to force out before committing, Force Pulse charging off your own casts, and E restated as a slow that self-peels backward.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit (catalogue defect 3), and dosFull[2].d offered a 'fifteen-second invitation' when Kassadin burns Riftwalk. Riftwalk's cooldown is 5/3.5/2 seconds.
audit.why: A fifteen-second window off a five-second ability is advice that gets the reader killed. The real punishable resource is mana, not cooldown: Null Sphere 60-80, Force Pulse 60-80, Riftwalk 40 and rising per repeat cast.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns now carries Riftwalk 5/3.5/2 with the escalating mana caveat, Force Pulse 21s, Null Sphere 650 range at 9s; the invitation is now his mana bar, not a fabricated cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[10] claimed the R zone 'traps the runback' and gave no account of Riftwalk as gank-escape.
audit.why: Riftwalk is 500 range on a 5-second cooldown at rank 1 for 40 mana. A gank lands only when he cannot pay for it.
audit.corrected: Gank advice keyed to his mana rather than to his cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: missingInteractions offers 'Kassadin's Null Sphere (Q) is a channel — your Between Worlds (R) cancels it outright.' That is backwards and I did not write it to the page.
audit.why: Riot's own Null Sphere text says it deals damage while 'interrupting channels' — Null Sphere interrupts channels, it is not itself one. The kit's derived 'channel' flag is a tooltip-parsing misfire, and the brief instructs that Riot's description wins over a contradicting flag.
audit.corrected: Not written. Recorded here so the rule does not get applied to another Kassadin matchup.

edits.before: Kassadin is arguably the weakest lane opponent you'll face at levels 1-5 — he has no mana to trade, minimal wave-clear, and Nether Blade doesn't proc often enough to matter yet. Twin Drift lets you poke him relentlessly without fear of retaliation, and The Weirding's slow punishes any hero attempt he makes to force a fight. Push hard, deny CS, and consider roaming since he can't punish your absence.

Poke his last-hits, slow him with E from 825 and hop back before Force Pulse charges. Push hard, deny CS, and roam with a shoved wave — Kassadin cannot punish your absence and cannot follow you fast enough to matter.

edits.before: Even with Riftwalk unlocked at 6, Kassadin still lacks the burst to threaten you — his damage only becomes real once he's stacked several Riftwalks and built into Void Stone. edits.before: This is the only window where Kassadin becomes dangerous — a fed Kassadin with a full mythic-tier build and Riftwalk stacks can blow you up out of nowhere with Silence-lock. Respect his all-in range past this point, ward around yourself in the late game, and don't get caught alone; otherwise your early lead should already have ended the game.

notes: Chart was split across layers on four of seven rows and the content chart gave Aurora 7/7 at a 47.68% win rate, which packet.defects already flags. Resolved to Aurora 0-5, Kassadin 6, with paired edits (full sides for rows 3-5, content win[6], ratings, and every affected why rewritten in the same proposal). Void Stone was written as an item in two content fields — it is Kassadin's passive (reduced magic damage, ignores unit collision), and that passive is a first-order fact in this matchup because Aurora is pure magic damage; it had never appeared on the page. 'Silence-lock' is not sourceable: Riot's Null Sphere text says it deals damage and interrupts channels, with no silence. breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit and dosFull[2].d claimed a fifteen-second Riftwalk window against a real 5/3.5/2 cooldown. missingInteractions rule 'Null Sphere is a channel — your R cancels it' is backwards (Null Sphere interrupts channels; the derived channel flag is a parsing misfire) and was NOT written. packet.suspectNames flags 'The Weirding's' in early as a probable wrong ability name — I rewrote that sentence for other reasons, so the flag is moot here, but I could not confirm or deny the name from the kit file, which carries no ability names for Aurora. Same reason I avoided 'Twin Drift' entirely and referred to Aurora's Q by slot and range.
